subject: Private deployment DPA — KMS & access boundary questions
messages:
From: Ivan Petrov <ivan.petrov@acmehealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Rao <proa@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA questions for private deployment - KMS / access boundaries

Diego / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we proceed to procurement, legal raised a couple of hard requirements about private deployment (VPC or on-prem) we need clarified on the DPA and ops side:

- Customer-managed keys: Acme requires we maintain custody of all encryption keys (we use a vendor-managed HSM). We need confirmation Redwood will not have key material or administrative access.
- Operator access: We allow limited operator activity for health checks and emergency troubleshooting, but only via jump host under our audit and with explicit temporary credentials. Please confirm typical operator access patterns and how those are logged.
- Subprocessors / vendors: We need a list of subprocessors that would touch metadata or logs for private deployments, and a commit to notice + approval process for adding them.
- Cross-border transfers: Our data residency is US-only; we need assurances any support staff or subprocessors outside the US do not receive customer data.
- Evidence: SOC 2 and penetration test reports are required for procurement.

Attached is our DPA checklist and a short network diagram. Can you point me to the Redwood DPA draft you intend to use for a VPC/on-prem engagement and any standard language for KMS handoffs?

Thanks,
Ivan
Ivan Petrov
CTO, Acme Health
ivan.petrov@acmehealth.com

Attachments: acme_dpa_checklist.pdf, acme_vpc_sketch.png

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Ivan Petrov <ivan.petrov@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <proa@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions for private deployment - KMS / access boundaries

Ivan — thanks for the clear list. I've looped in our legal and solutions folks (cc'd). High-level answers below; Marissa will propose DPA text.

- Customer-managed keys: We support customer-managed KMS for both VPC and on-prem deployments. Redwood will not store private key material. Operationally we perform a one-time "KMS handshake" to configure encryption envelopes; we do not have blind access to keys. I attach our KMS handshake matrix to show roles and actions.
- Operator access: Our standard is zero standing access to customer disks/keys. Support jumps use short-lived credentials and are performed via customer-controlled bastion or a ticketed remote session with session recording. All sessions produce audit logs shipped to your monitoring endpoint (or retained in-place per your retention policy).
- Subprocessors: For private deployments we only use a small set of subprocessors (monitoring partner, artifact distribution CDN for agent updates). We'll provide a current list and a 30-day notice + opt-out mechanism for changes in the DPA.
- Cross-border: For US-only accounts we pin routing and support to US regions and staff; any exception requires written approval.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report and pentest summary are available; we can provide redacted artifacts under NDA.

Next steps I suggest: Marissa will send proposed DPA language for the KMS and operator-access clauses. If acceptable, we can spin up a short SOW covering onboarding steps and a timeline for the KMS handshake.

Attaching: redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf, kms_handshake_matrix.xlsx, network_diagram_acme_vpc.png

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ivan Petrov <ivan.petrov@acmehealth.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Rao <proa@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions for private deployment - KMS / access boundaries

Ivan / Priya / Diego — thanks. I reviewed Diego's summary and attached an initial set of redlines for the DPA focused on private deployments. High-level points and proposed clause language: 

1) Key custody and access
Proposed excerpt: "Customer retains sole custody and control of encryption keys. Redwood shall not have administrative access to key material, plaintext encryption keys, or customer key vault credentials. Any cryptographic handshake necessary for service operation shall be performed without transferring key material to Redwood and under mutually agreed operational controls."

2) Operator & emergency access
Proposed excerpt: "Redwood personnel shall have no standing administrative access to Customer data. Emergency access may be granted only via a Customer-controlled temporary access mechanism (e.g., bastion+jump host) and shall require documented approval from an authorized Customer representative. All emergency sessions will be recorded and audit logs exported to Customer-controlled storage within 24 hours."

3) Subprocessors and notice
Proposed excerpt: "Redwood shall provide a current list of subprocessors and thirty (30) days' prior written notice for additions. For Private Deployments, Customer may object to new subprocessors, and Redwood will offer commercially reasonable mitigations or the option to terminate the affected service component."

4) Data transfer & residency
Proposed excerpt: "Processing and support activities for Customer data shall be performed in the geographic region specified in the Order Form. Any exception that results in cross-border transfer of Customer data requires prior written consent and appropriate transfer mechanisms (e.g., SCCs)."

5) Evidence & audits
Proposed excerpt: "Redwood shall provide SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted penetration test summary under NDA. Redwood will support customer-requested audits to the extent described in the DPA and SOW."

Questions for Acme: which KMS vendor / HSM are you using (vendor & whether you require an HSM-backed API)? Also confirm whether you require Redwood to sign a separate KMS operator attestation (we can provide one).

Diego — if Ivan confirms, I can push a redlined PDF and tracked changes to DocuSign for Priya to review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ivan Petrov <ivan.petrov@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions for private deployment - KMS / access boundaries

Marissa / Diego — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- KMS vendor: We use Thales Luna HSM for key custody. We require an HSM-backed API and do not permit key import into third-party KMSes.
- Model artifacts: We must ensure that Redwood does not retain model-provided customer artifacts (prompts, training uploads). Please add explicit "no retention" language for customer-provided artifacts and inference inputs/outputs unless explicitly part of a logging opt-in.
- Subprocessors: We need to see current subprocessor list before legal signs; 30-day notice is acceptable.

We'd prefer a short call to walk through the redlines and the handshake steps. Are you available tomorrow at 10am ET?

Thanks,
Ivan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ivan Petrov <ivan.petrov@acmehealth.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <proa@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions for private deployment - KMS / access boundaries

Ivan — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Operationally we can meet tomorrow at 10am ET. To make the call productive, I'm sharing a short onboarding ops playbook and the tasks we'll run during the KMS handshake: 

- Pre-call: exchange KMS vendor docs (API spec) and network ACLs.
- Step 1 (KMS handshake): generate key-encryption-key (KEK) wrapped by your HSM; Redwood receives only wrapped KEK and config metadata. No plaintext key material ever leaves your HSM.
- Step 2 (Agent deployment): agent bundles delivered via signed artifact from Redwood CDN; CRC checks and signature verification.
- Step 3 (Support model): no standing access; emergency support uses customer-initiated session with just-in-time role elevation; session ids and recordings exported to your S3/GCS bucket.
- Step 4 (Audit & evidence): provide SOC 2 Type II, pentest summary, recent change log of subprocessors.

I'll share the playbook doc on the call and follow up with a short SOW template and a DocuSign-ready redline from Marissa after your confirmation. Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567-RWI-ACME-47 and DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/next-step/acme-dpa-draft

See you tomorrow — dialing details to follow.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
